criteria.sufficiency: Executable legacy-parity cases plus the unchanged public suite on candidate versus parent show omitted workflowWorkspace behaves as before and historical records keep meaning.
Real load and preflight over disposable Git repositories show a distinct docs repository owning the workflow directory while source and methodology stay separate.
Each listed preflight defect is refused in isolation against a passing twin, proving the refusal is attributable to that defect.
Inspecting recorded allocations and bindings, with guard-mutation sensitivity, establishes repository-qualified commit/path/content provenance and the retained source/docs pair.
Per-failure-mode refusals (wrong repo, stale binding, content, ancestry) shown to depend on the guard by mutation in a scratch clone.
Partial single-repository checkpoints are shown to yield no transition and no combined-success claim while the docs ledger alone decides state.
Attempted source writes by docs-authoring roles are refused through real containment and their artifacts resolve from docs commits.
Attempted direct docs writes and private reads by Implementation are refused while the host-brokered evidence action still completes.
Evaluator roles show private isolation, no source write, host-owned results and eligible promotion landing in docs.
Deterministic integration runs resolve As-Built, acceptance, Outcome, correction and recovery inputs from split repositories with no new authority kind.
Effective grants carry the per-workspace access map, fail closed without it, and wrong-root writes and ungranted Git actions are refused at launch and attach.
Diff and search inspection of the candidate shows no push, credential exposure, second ledger, migration or atomicity claim, with the suite showing no regression.
Following the shipped example verbatim on clean disposable checkouts shows preflight passing without Harness code edits.
Committed real-provider smoke evidence is checked against each element of the criterion, rejecting mock or readiness-only substitutes.
Contract version and forward-only adoption records plus named trusted runtime/methodology revisions show no candidate self-authorization.
